title: Not a coder: I built and launched a Roblox Halloween game in 3 days with Claude + Roblox Studio’s MCP
author: Mages17
selftext:
I’m a sales manager, not a programmer. Over 3 days I made Lantern Patch, a cozy pumpkin-carving clicker on Roblox, by talking to Claude, which drives Roblox Studio through its built-in MCP server.

What worked: Claude writes one build script that rebuilds the whole place, then runs an automatic playtest (50 checks plus a phone-screen check) before I’m allowed to publish. Before launch, AI “testers” with different personas (a kid, a pro simulator player, a reward psychologist) played it and wrote reports, and their fixes went in.

What didn’t: art from 4 agents blew the phone performance budget, so we added a hard limit. And the AI missed a real bug I found in 5 minutes on my phone: you could walk off the edge of the map.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow. The game is free to try (16+ for now): [https://www.roblox.com/games/123618562322847](https://www.roblox.com/games/123618562322847)

Question for you all: has anyone else used AI playtesters? Mine caught a lot of balance problems, but missed the one bug a human found in 5 minutes. I’m curious whether that matches your experience.
